We account for income taxes under the asset and liability method, which requires the recognition of deferred tax assets and liabilities for the expected future tax consequences of events that have been included in the financial statements.

Under this method, we determine deferred tax assets and liabilities on the basis of the differences between the financial statement and tax bases of assets and liabilities by using enacted tax rates in effect for the year in which the differences are expected to reverse.

In making such a determination, we consider all available positive and negative evidence, including future reversals of existing taxable temporary differences, projected future taxable income, tax-planning strategies, and results of recent operations.

estimates.t: Our discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations are based upon our interim condensed consolidated financial statements, which have been prepared in accordance with GAAP.

estimates.name: Restricted Cash
estimates.t: Restricted cash primarily consists of funds held in segregated accounts pursuant to contractual arrangements and is not available for general corporate purposes.

estimates.name: Fixed Assets Not In Service
estimates.t: Fixed assets not yet placed into service consist of costs incurred to acquire, construct, or develop long-lived assets that are not yet ready for their intended use and are recorded within equipment, net.

estimates.name: Intangible Assets, net
estimates.t: Definite-lived intangible assets are amortized on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives.

estimates.name: Stock-Based Compensation
estimates.t: We account for stock-based compensation in accordance with ASC 718 , Compensation - Stock Compensation .

estimates.name: Income Taxes
estimates.t: See Note 3 - Summary of Significant Accounting Policies and Note 19 – Income Taxes of accompanying interim condensed consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this Form 10-Q for information related to the change in tax status of Boost Run in connection with the Business Combination.

statements.t: “We expect to have all existing contracts connected to our $2.7 billion in TCV deployed in 2027, with 26% of it live by the end of this month.

Given our model, each project adds positive incremental cash flow starting in month one of being fully deployed, and we expect to achieve sustainable net cash flow margins of 15-20% in forward periods.

Importantly, we have no dilutive debt or warrant overhang, and our financing is project-specific and paid down every month out of contracted customer cash flows and 100% structured to pay down inside the contract term.

Our customer base spans some of the best known, well-capitalized compute intensive participants in the AI ecosystem, engaged with us under long-term contracts, and we look forward to growing alongside them.”

“With $157 million in unrestricted cash at quarter-end and continued access to non-dilutive project financing, we remain focused on disciplined capital deployment, maintaining financial flexibility and converting our growing contracted revenue portfolio intro recurring revenue and cash flow.”

risks.t: (i) the Company’s ability to execute on contracted revenue
(ii) changes in customer demand or contract cancellations
(iii) supply chain disruptions, including GPU availability
(iv) the Company’s reliance on relationships with NVIDIA and other key partners
(v) general economic and market conditions, including interest rates and inflation
(vi) regulatory changes affecting the data center or AI industries
(vii) competition in the cloud infrastructure market
(viii) execution risks related to facility expansion and deployment
(ix) other risks detailed in the Company’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission
